propositions: Merge-abort recovery logic for tracking and restoring untracked/local files is duplicated across sync.py and push_recovery.py, with divergent implementations and missing guards.
The quarantine mover in push_recovery.py checks for tracked files via git status before moving, but sync.py's mover lacks this fence, causing tracked data to be at risk of relocation.
Both sync and push_recovery need different git execution paths (module-level vs late-bound seams), preventing direct code sharing without a neutral, callable-accepting interface.
A single merge_recovery.py module consolidates the shared parser and mover, accepting git as a plain callable parameter to serve both sync and push_recovery callers.
The untracked-file fence (??-check) is extended to sync.py and doctor.py paths for the first time, with no observable behavior change on existing callers.
